title: "Building the site from primary sources"
date: 2026-08-04
date-modified: 2026-09-30
---

bioconductor.org's pages are built by
[bioc-website](https://github.com/seandavi/bioconductor-website): a Python pipeline that
fetches data from primary sources into `astro/data/`, and an Astro build that renders it.
Since the 2026-09-28 cutover the `bioc-site` Worker serves this build first on every path
and falls back to the mirror (the R2 copy of the legacy site) where the build has no file.
This page describes how a build reaches production, how a content edit gets there, and what
the build does not cover yet. The measurements from the August build are kept further down
as a [dated record](#the-2026-08-04-build-record).

Companion pages: [Reproducing the package pages](reproducing-package-pages.qmd) for the
data-source analysis, [Edge cache](cache.qmd) for caching and purges,
[CI & scheduled jobs](ci.qmd) for the other workflows.

## How a build reaches production

`.github/workflows/site.yml` in bioc-website runs on every push to `main`:

1. Run the pipeline's unit tests (`pipeline/test_*.py`). The pipeline itself does not run.
2. Pull the data snapshot `s3://bioc-site/_ci/site-data.tar.zst` from R2 and unpack it into
   `astro/`.
3. `npm run build`, which is `astro build && pagefind --site dist`.
4. Upload `astro/dist` to `site/<sha>/` in the `bioc-site` bucket, then write `<sha>` to
   `site/latest`.

The Worker does the rest. Its route table `_routes.json` is
`{"build":"latest","prefixes":["/"]}`: every path tries `site/<latest sha>/` first, then the
mirror. The Worker caches the `site/latest` pointer for 60 seconds per isolate. Build pages
are edge-cached under keys that contain the build sha, so a new build needs no purge. Every
response served from the build carries an `x-bioc-build: <sha>` header; a page without that
header came from the mirror.

| Measured 2026-09-29 (run for `360bb87`) | |
|---|---|
| Pull snapshot | 5 s |
| Astro build + Pagefind | 27 s |
| Upload to `site/<sha>/` | 17 min 43 s |
| Whole run | 19 min |
| Published build | 17,787 files, 254 MiB |

The run before it (`de0c708`, same day) took 11 min 30 s; the upload is most of the time and
varies. The build is small because CI builds only the live releases (3.23 and 3.24), the prose
pages and `/next/`. Releases 2.5 to 3.22 are archival
([ADR 0006](adr/0006-old-releases-and-their-checkresults-are-archival.md)) and are served
from the mirror.

**Rollback.** Set `"build"` in `_routes.json` to an earlier sha instead of `"latest"`, or
write the earlier sha to `site/latest`. Either reaches every isolate within 60 seconds.
Earlier builds stay in R2 (12 `site/<sha>/` prefixes on 2026-09-30); there is no retention
policy yet ([bioc-website#2](https://github.com/seandavi/bioconductor-website/issues/2)).

### The data snapshot

CI does not fetch from primary sources. It builds from a snapshot of `astro/data/` (the live
releases plus `site/`) and `astro/public/`, made by running the pipeline on a workstation and
uploading the result, as the bioc-website README describes:

```sh
just data
tar -C astro -cf - data/site data/3.23 data/3.24 public | zstd -T0 -8 \
  | rclone rcat r2:bioc-site/_ci/site-data.tar.zst
```

The refresh is manual and no one is named to do it; scheduling it is
[bioc-website#5](https://github.com/seandavi/bioconductor-website/issues/5) (open). The
snapshot in use is 30 MB, uploaded 2026-09-29 12:40 UTC. The one before it dated from
2026-08-13. The full 35-release data, including the 2.5 to 3.22 snapshot that no live source
can regenerate, is `_ci/site-data-full.tar.zst` (2026-08-13).

Two things follow from the snapshot:

- A change to `pipeline/*.py` reaches production only when someone regenerates and uploads
  the snapshot. Merging it changes nothing served.
- Package landing pages for 3.23 and 3.24 show the version and download links from the
  repository's own `PACKAGES` indexes as they were when the snapshot was made
  ([bioc-website#31](https://github.com/seandavi/bioconductor-website/pull/31)). The hourly
  `bioc-sync` updates the package files themselves; it does not update the landing pages.

`/next/` pages are different: the Astro build fetches bioc-registry's propagation index over
HTTP while it runs, so they are as current as the last build on `main`.

### Previews

Every pull request is built the same way and uploaded to `preview/pr-<n>/` in R2. The URL is
`https://bioc-dev.cancerdatasci.org/_pr/<n>/`; CI posts it as a comment on the PR, and
`preview-cleanup.yml` deletes the prefix when the PR closes. The R2 key and the URL path
differ (`preview/pr-<n>/` versus `/_pr/<n>/`). `/_pr/<n>/` also answers on
bioconductor.org today ([bioc-edge#48](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/issues/48)).
Internal links in a preview are root-absolute and leave the preview
([bioc-website#4](https://github.com/seandavi/bioconductor-website/issues/4)).

## Editing content: where, and how long it takes

| To change | Edit | Reaches bioconductor.org |
|---|---|---|
| Layout, components, `/next/` pages | a PR to bioc-website | on the next `main` build after merge |
| Pipeline code (how data is fetched or transformed) | a PR to bioc-website | after the merge, a snapshot refresh **and** a `main` build |
| Prose pages (text of `/about/`, `/help/`, `/developers/`, ...) | [Bioconductor/bioconductor.org](https://github.com/Bioconductor/bioconductor.org), as before | after a snapshot refresh **and** a `main` build |
| Package titles, descriptions, maintainers | the package's own `DESCRIPTION` | after a snapshot refresh **and** a `main` build |

The prose still lives in Bioconductor/bioconductor.org, which the core team edits. The pipeline
reads it when the snapshot is made. A one-time import of the prose into bioc-website is
planned in its `CONTRIBUTING.md`; there is no tracking issue or date for it.

Latency, once someone acts:

- **Snapshot refresh.** No automatic trigger. After uploading a new snapshot, a build must
  run: `site.yml` runs only on push and pull request, so either push to `main` or re-run the
  latest `main` run (`gh run rerun`).
- **Build.** 11 to 19 minutes on the two runs measured 2026-09-29.
- **Serving.** Up to 60 seconds for the Worker to see the new pointer, and up to 5 minutes
  for browsers holding the old page (build pages are sent with
  `cache-control: public, max-age=300, s-maxage=31536000`).

A prose edit merged upstream today is therefore not live until the next manual refresh, which
has no schedule.

### Divergences from upstream

Wherever the build renders Bioconductor/bioconductor.org content differently from nanoc, or
works around something in it, bioc-website records it in
[`UPSTREAM.md`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioconductor-website/blob/main/UPSTREAM.md), with
the upstream change that would remove the workaround. Any PR that changes
`pipeline/content.py` updates that file. It is the list to work through before the prose moves
into bioc-website.

## The seam

Two halves that do not know about each other:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  RU["r-universe API<br/>(software metadata)"] --> P
  PK["PACKAGES indexes<br/>on bioconductor.org<br/>(versions, downloads)"] --> P
  TB["source tarballs<br/>(DESCRIPTION)"] --> P
  GH["Bioconductor/bioconductor.org<br/>git repo (prose)"] --> P
  BV["Bioconductor/biocViews<br/>vocabulary"] --> P
  CR["CRAN PACKAGES"] --> P
  WS["/packages/stats/<br/>(Rank, via master)"] -.-> P
  P["./bioc.py<br/>pipeline"] --> D["astro/data/"]
  D --> S["R2: _ci/site-data.tar.zst<br/>(uploaded by hand)"]
  S --> A["CI: astro build<br/>+ Pagefind"]
  REG["bioc-registry<br/>propagation index"] -->|/next/ only| A
  A --> O["R2: site/&lt;sha&gt;/"]
  O --> W["bioc-site Worker"]

  classDef ok fill:#f3fbf4,stroke:#3d8b47,color:#12263f
  classDef q fill:#fff8e8,stroke:#b8860b,color:#12263f
  class RU,PK,TB,GH,BV,CR,P,D,A,O,W,REG ok
  class WS,S q
```

The pipeline decides *where data comes from*; the Astro build decides *how it is rendered*.
`astro/data/` is the contract between them. Locally, everything is driven from one CLI, with
`just` recipes over the top:

```bash
just data          # fetch the live releases from primary sources
just build         # astro build + Pagefind index -> astro/dist/
just coverage      # compare against bioconductor.org
```

`just coverage` still requests `https://bioconductor.org` (`SITE` in `pipeline/coverage.py`).
Since 2026-09-28 that host serves this build first, so coverage no longer compares against an
independent legacy site. For pages the build lacks, it still measures the mirror.

## What the build does not cover

Checked 2026-09-30 against the snapshot and build `360bb87`:

- **17 prose pages with ERB the pipeline cannot evaluate.** The pipeline flags them
  `erbUnresolved` and does not render them, so the Worker serves the mirror copy. Three need
  build or live services (`/dashboard/`, `/developers/help_wanted/`, `/developers/gitlog/`),
  four need data the pipeline could supply (`/developers/new_packages/`,
  `/about/annual-reports/`, `/about/mirrors/`, `/help/publications/`), and ten are under
  `/help/course-materials/`: the index page and the nine year pages 2010 to 2018, which are
  all blocked on the `_course_year_summary` partial.
- **`/help/events/` shows raw ERB.** Its two `<%= render(...)` calls span two lines each, the
  single-line detector misses them, and the page is built with the tags as text. The live page
  (from build `360bb87`) shows both. No open bioc-website issue covers it.
- **`Rank`** is read from `/packages/stats/` on bioconductor.org, which the Worker passes
  through to master uncached. It depends on master until download statistics have another
  home.
- **Check results, vignettes, manuals** and the other per-package artifacts are served from the
  mirror; the build does not produce them.
- **Search.** Site search is a Pagefind index built from `dist/` at build time (bioc-website
  `1c92ffb`, 2026-08-14): 4,445 files in build `360bb87`. There is no server-side search;
  `/solr` is not served.

## The 2026-08-04 build (record)

The sections below are the measurements and findings from the first full build, 2026-08-04 to
2026-08-13, which rebuilt all 35 releases. They are kept as written except where marked
*(corrected 2026-09-30)*. CI today builds only the live releases (above).

### What it produces

| Page type | Built | Recall | Source |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| Package landing pages | 92,142 | 100% | packages.json |
| Prose pages | 518 | 96.8% | the site's git repo |
| Package index pages | 123 | 100% | packages.json |
| biocViews browsers | 35 | 100% | tree.json |
| Images / CSS / JS | 361 | — | copied verbatim |

The full build then was 93,186 files in about 50 seconds; with the `/next/` pages (below),
97,001 files in about 60 seconds. Both figures predate the Pagefind index.

Recall is measured per page type deliberately. A single percentage over a corpus that is 99%
package pages would read as ~100% while every prose page was missing.

Precision was checked in the other direction: 30 sampled URLs of each type, all of which
resolved on the live site. Nothing is invented. A 200 on a page the real site does not have
would be a silent wrong answer rather than a visible gap.

### The tarball origin

The largest change. Annotation, experiment and workflow packages (1,387 of them, about a
third of the corpus) previously had no origin except VIEWS on the site being rebuilt. Their
real origin is `DESCRIPTION` inside the source tarball: the maintainer's own file, passed
through the repository untouched.

The naive version of this downloads 1,387 tarballs, several of them hundreds of megabytes, to
read a few hundred bytes from each. Instead: `DESCRIPTION` sits near the front of the archive,
gzip is a stream, and R2 serves ranged requests, so a 64 KB ranged GET, inflated as far as it
goes, is enough. Bounded at 64 KB regardless of package size, roughly 0.1 s each, the whole
corpus in about 50 seconds.

Two findings that only appear once you run it:

**VIEWS appends the repository's root biocViews term.** A software package declaring only
`DifferentialExpression` is published as `["DifferentialExpression", "Software"]`. Packages
never declare that term themselves (it comes from which repository they were built into), so
any generator reading DESCRIPTION or r-universe has to add it back. Without it, biocViews
disagreed on 89% of packages and the category browser lost all four of its top-level roots.
With it, overall field agreement against the published data goes from 90.8% to **98.9%**.

**Not every archive is ordered with DESCRIPTION near the front.** 32 of 928 annotation
packages put a large `.rda` first (`BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg17` leads with `chr13.rda`), and
gzip cannot be read backwards, so no affordable prefix reaches them. Those still fall back to
VIEWS and are named in `provenance.json` rather than absorbed silently.

#### What the residual 1.1% is

Of 480 disagreeing fields out of 41,844:

- **~230 whitespace only.** DESCRIPTION wraps prose across lines; unfolding differs by a space.
- **~110 version drift.** r-universe tracks the release *branch head*; the published VIEWS is a
  frozen snapshot. `AnVILWorkflow` is 1.12.0 upstream-of-record and 1.11.0 as published. This
  is a real semantic difference and matters for any rebuild that claims to reproduce a release
  rather than track it. (Since bioc-website#31, 2026-09-29, software landing pages take their
  version from the repository's `PACKAGES` index instead.)
- **~125 absent in ours**, concentrated in about 16 packages.
- **A handful where our value is right and the published one is wrong.** `BubbleTree`'s
  published `Title` is the literal string `ERROR`; `ViSEAGO`'s published `License` is
  `GPL-3 bioconductor.org`, with a following field leaked into it.

### Deliberate divergences

**The biocViews browser is rendered at build time.** Upstream ships a near-empty page and
builds the tree client-side with a jsTree widget that fetches `tree.json` over XHR. This
renders the same 500 nodes as nested `<details>`. Same data, same `#___Software` anchors that
the header and footer link to directly, but crawlable, JS-free, and not dependent on a second
request succeeding. *(Corrected 2026-09-30:* since 2026-08-14 the page's main interface is a
hydrated React package finder (`PackageFinder`, the site's only island); the `<details>` tree
is the fallback when JavaScript or the island does not load, and is hidden once it does.*)*

**jQuery is served locally.** Upstream pulls jQuery 1.5.1 (2011) from `ajax.googleapis.com` on
the `rebase` path; the same file is already vendored at `/js/jquery.js`. Same library, one
fewer third-party origin.

**highlight.js is not loaded from cdnjs.** Nothing should need a CDN to be up in order to
render.

Divergences in the prose pipeline are now recorded in bioc-website's `UPSTREAM.md`
([above](#divergences-from-upstream)).

### ERB is resolved in the pipeline, not ported by hand

Most of the surviving ERB is trivially evaluable, and treating it as a wall costs pages
needlessly: the homepage is eight lines of nothing but static partial includes. The pipeline
therefore expands the constructs that occur:

```
<%= config[:key] %>          site-config lookup, optionally .sub()'d
<%= render('/partial/') %>   static partial, expanded inline, recursive
<%= ami_url(...) %>          a one-line link builder in lib/helpers.rb
```

Anything else is left in place and reported per page as `erbUnresolved`, so *whether a page can
render* is decided once, in the pipeline, and the renderer just obeys. An earlier hardcoded
exclusion list in the Astro side went stale the moment the resolver improved.

Partials that loop over build data cannot be expanded this way (that data belongs to the
renderer), so they become **named slots**. `_top_events` is the first: the pipeline emits
`<!--slot:events-->` and Astro fills it from the same `events.json` it already writes. An
explicit slot means a page that needs one cannot silently render without it.

**Detecting ERB is easy to get wrong in both directions.** The first attempt counted bare `<%`
with no closing `%>`, which flagged a 6,973-line release-notes page containing no ERB at all:
the matches were R's `%<%` operator quoted in package NEWS text. It also used a
more-than-two-tags threshold, which let ten pages with one or two *real* tags reach the build
and ship visible `<% %>` to readers. The fix requires `<%...%>` on a single line. Prose recall
fell from a reported 97.9% to 96.8% when this was fixed, and no page in `dist/` then contained a
visible ERB tag, where ten had. *(Corrected 2026-09-30:* this page said every ERB tag in the
content tree is single-line. It is not: `/help/events/` has two multi-line `render()` calls,
which the detector misses and which ship as visible text; see
[What the build does not cover](#what-the-build-does-not-cover).*)*

### What was still missing on 2026-08-04

- **17 prose pages with ERB the pipeline cannot evaluate.** Still 17 on 2026-09-30; the
  current list is [above](#what-the-build-does-not-cover).
- **33 of 35 releases still use snapshotted data.** Only 3.23 and 3.24 had been regenerated
  from primary sources; r-universe holds only release and devel. *(Since settled: releases
  2.5 to 3.22 are archival per
  [ADR 0006](adr/0006-old-releases-and-their-checkresults-are-archival.md) and served from the
  mirror.)*
- **`hasNEWS` / `hasREADME` / `hasINSTALL` / `hasLICENSE`, `vignettes`, `Rfiles`** for the three
  tarball-sourced repositories. These are whole-archive facts and the 64 KB prefix cannot see
  them. They are reported as unavailable rather than guessed: defaulting them to `false` would
  silently drop documentation links from ~1,400 landing pages.
- **`Rank`** had no independent path: bio-web-stats was reachable only because master
  reverse-proxies it.
- **Search.** Solr was out of scope. *(Since 2026-08-14 the build ships a Pagefind index.)*
- **checkResults, vignette and manual files.** Static artifacts already in R2; the Worker serves
  them, the build does not produce them.

### Next-generation pages from the build-system data plane (added 2026-08-13)

Everything above reproduces the *existing* site from its existing data contract. A second
track renders pages the legacy build never produced, from a data source the legacy pipeline
never had:

- **`/next/{universe}/checkResults.html`**: a check-results matrix per universe (release and
  devel), built from the propagation pipeline's archived observations: per-configuration
  verdicts for every package, worst-first, with a column showing what
  [the propagation gate](propagation-gate.qmd) let through. nanoc never built check pages
  (they arrive in the docroot from the build system), so this is new rendering, not a port.
- **`/next/{universe}/package/{pkg}.html`**: one landing page per entry in bioc-registry's
  propagation index, rendered through the **same component as the parity build** via a
  mapping from the registry's metadata into the existing `packages.json` contract. Legacy JSON
  and the new data plane feed identical rendering. Version truth comes from the gate, not the
  latest build; downloads point at the gate's content-addressed artifacts; per-architecture
  availability follows the gate's per-arch decisions. Build `360bb87` (2026-09-29) has 2,418
  pages for `bioc` and 2,390 for `bioc-release`, one per index entry including seeded ones.
- The `/next/` pages carry their own clean-slate layout (system fonts, dark-mode aware, no
  jQuery, no legacy CSS cascade), with the rendering stance settled for the redesign:
  **content is static HTML; reactivity is layered over it** (a copy button, table filtering)
  as progressive enhancement. Landing and check pages are cited, curled and archived
  documents; they are never a client-rendered application.

*(Corrected 2026-09-30:* title, description, authors and vignettes come from the metadata
bioc-registry archives in its propagation index (bioc-website `cf759fa`, 2026-08-13), so they
describe the propagated version. The build asks r-universe only for downloads, stars and
reverse-dependency counts and for the banner shown when r-universe has a newer version, and
an r-universe outage leaves those out rather than failing the build.*)*

The `/next/` pages are a preview of pages built from bioc-registry data. bioconductor.org's own
package pages do not use it; switching them is part of the
[registry switch](registry-switch.qmd) plan.
